profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at an industrial ML research lab evaluating a proposal to reproduce and extend a paper on neural-network-assisted Collaborative Optimization for multidisciplinary aircraft design. The team has a draft implementation plan for a surrogate classifier that uses boundary-distance information to accelerate convergence in decomposed optimization, and this meeting is meant to judge whether the plan is sufficiently specified to begin a two-week prototype sprint. The agenda is to review the benchmark setup, the intended labeling scheme for the classifier, the fairness of the baseline comparison, and what evidence is needed for sign-off. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on the prototype plan plus a short list of assumed implementation details for the engineering handoff.

members.name: Dr. Lina Moreau
members.expertise: Multidisciplinary design optimization, collaborative optimization, surrogate modeling for engineering systems
members.background: Lina has a PhD in aerospace engineering and has led several internal studies on decomposition methods for aircraft conceptual design; she is reviewing the proposal mainly for methodological faithfulness to the published approach.
members.private_state: She wants the prototype to stay close to the paper so that any convergence gains can be defensibly attributed to the asymmetric-loss classifier design rather than to benchmark or infrastructure changes; she is also trying to avoid a sprawling implementation that would delay a publication-quality reproduction.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'distance to the boundary,' it refers to a signed, normalized distance in each discipline's local feasibility space because that is the only interpretation she sees as faithful to the paper's classifier formulation.
When people say 'the aircraft case,' they mean the published low-cost aircraft Collaborative Optimization benchmark used in the paper before any internal high-fidelity variant is considered.
A 'same-budget' comparison in collaborative optimization means the same number of outer coordination iterations, since that is the conventional unit in the optimization literature she works in.

A prototype is 'ready for review' once there is one clean end-to-end reproduction on the toy example and one aircraft run showing the convergence trend, even if seed-to-seed stability has not been fully characterized.

members.name: Ethan Park
members.role: Staff Research Engineer, ML Systems for Scientific Computing
members.expertise: Training pipelines, differentiable simulation interfaces, benchmark infrastructure, experimental reproducibility
members.background: Ethan has an ML systems background and maintains the lab's optimization benchmark stack, including the internal aircraft design environment with automatic derivative extraction and distributed experiment runners.
members.private_state: He wants to anchor the prototype in the lab's existing benchmark and evaluation pipeline so the implementation can be reused later; he is also trying to protect the team from approving a result that looks good in a single run but does not hold up under standard reproducibility checks.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'distance to the boundary,' it can be instantiated using the global consistency-violation geometry already available in the internal pipeline, because he treats the exact coordinate space as an implementation detail rather than a conceptual choice.

When people say 'the aircraft case,' they mean the lab's internal aircraft benchmark with existing discipline wrappers and derivative hooks, since that is the default aircraft setup everyone has been using recently.

A 'same-budget' comparison means the same total compute expenditure, including surrogate retraining overhead, failed restarts, and inner solves, because otherwise the engineering comparison is not operationally fair.

A design is not 'ready' unless it can be run through the standard evaluation harness with multiple seeds and produce stable summary tables, even if the underlying method is already conceptually settled.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of 'boundary distance' in the classifier labels
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'use the boundary distance and derivative for the infeasible class.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means a signed, normalized distance to each discipline-specific feasibility boundary inside the local subproblem space used by Collaborative Optimization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the distance derived from the global consistency-violation boundary available in the shared aircraft benchmark representation, effectively in the coupled design space used by the existing pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from the paper and sounds fully specified on the surface, so each assumes the other is simply referring to the obvious paper-defined construct without needing to unpack the coordinate space or sign convention.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss 'starting with the aircraft case from the proposal.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the published, low-dimensional aircraft benchmark associated with the paper's original demonstration and suitable for a faithful reproduction.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the lab's internal aircraft benchmark that uses the same disciplinary split idea but has different fidelity, variable count, and existing software interfaces.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both benchmarks are casually referred to inside the team as 'the aircraft case,' and because both are legitimate aircraft MDO examples with similar disciplinary language, neither expects ambiguity in the reference.

misalignment_points.topic: How to judge a 'same-budget' baseline comparison
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the new method should beat baseline CO 'under the same budget.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will judge fairness by matching the number of outer Collaborative Optimization coordination iterations and then comparing convergence behavior across those iterations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will judge fairness by matching total wall-clock or cluster-hour usage, counting surrogate training, data generation, and restart overhead as part of the budget.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In design reviews, 'same budget' sounds like a standard fairness requirement, and each person's criterion is conventional in their own subcommunity, so the phrase creates false consensus rather than triggering clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about whether the design is 'ready for sign-off' after the prototype sprint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means one successful end-to-end implementation that reproduces the toy example and demonstrates the expected convergence pattern on the aircraft case.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means the method has been run through the standard evaluation harness with multiple seeds and enough automation to produce stable summary tables for internal comparison.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the normal design-review language of readiness and sign-off, but each silently imports their own standard of completeness from research validation versus engineering reproducibility.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this prototype tightly scoped. If we drift from the published setup, any improvement will be impossible to attribute cleanly to the asymmetric-loss classifier idea. The review should stay centered on whether the implementation preserves the paper's collaborative optimization structure and label construction, not on building a generalized platform.

turns.inner_thought: If this can't run through our existing benchmark and evaluation harness, we'll pay for it twice later. I also don't want a one-off demo that people call done and then can't reproduce. Readiness, to me, means it fits the standard pipeline from the start, even if the first sprint is narrow.
